title: Julius Defranceschi
eyebrow: born 1879 · k. u. k. Kriegsmarine · 1894 to 1918
dek: A complete officer's career, transcribed from 181 entries across 79 volumes of the Austro-Hungarian navy lists. Twenty-four years, from a first-year cadet at the naval academy to a name still on the active list four months before the empire ended. He is not proved kin to this family — and everything below is documented to the page.
lede: This archive found him on 13 September 2026, on the day it first opened Hungaricana. He was the largest single thing in it: **196 hits on one man**, and nobody had ever looked.

The navy lists are the best serial source a family historian can be handed. They were printed two to four times a year, they name every officer, and they say where each one was standing. Run them end to end and a life falls out of them — which is what follows.

**Read the warning first.** Nothing here proves that Julius belongs to the Kvarner households on this site. What is known is that he is of the name, born in the right decade, and serving in the navy of the empire whose harbour master at Fiume was also a Defranceschi. That is a strong circumstantial setting and it is not a descent. **His birthplace is not given in any of the 181 entries**, and until it is, he stands on this site as documented and unjoined.

facts.s: Given in the seniority lists of 1915, 1917 and 1918, all three agreeing.
«Dient seit 1./7. 98» — the date his academy class was commissioned.
Peers in the same table carry A, T, M, F and OB; his is A alone.
Still on the active officer list, four months before the empire dissolved.

career.what: **First year at the naval academy.** He appears under *Marine-Behörden, Commanden und Anstalten* in the **1. Jahrgang** — the first-year class — between Cvitkovich, Emerich and Fautz, Gustav Ritter von. He would have been fifteen.
career.cite: Rangs- und Eintheilungs-Liste der k. u. k. Kriegs-Marine, 15.11.1894, p. 134

career.what: **Commissioned.** The service date carried beside his name for the next twenty years. Four years after the first-year list, which is the length of the course.
**Seekadett.** Listed under the rank with Fauz, Gustav Ritter von, immediately after the Linienschiffsfähnriche.

**Linienschiffsfähnrich, and head of the harbour depot.** *«Matrosendetachement. Komdt. L. Sch. L. Ferro, Raimund Ritt. v. (Leiter des Hafendepots) L. Sch. F. Defranceschi, Julius.»* The same page lists the **Werfte S. Marco** — the San Marco yard at Trieste. A harbour master's name, running a harbour depot.
career.cite: Rangs- und Eintheilungs-Liste, 14.06.1904, p. 147; repeated 15.11.1904, p. 149

career.what: **Linienschiffsleutnant, commanding a patrol boat on the Danube.** Under the heading **DONAUFLOTTILLE**: *«Patrouillenboot, 15 T., 300 ind. Pfk., 1 G. In Dienst gestellt seit 8. Oktober 1908. L. Sch. L. Defranceschi, Julius.»* Fifteen tons, three hundred indicated horsepower, one gun, in commission since the previous October. He has left the sea for the river.

**Aboard the armoured cruiser «Kaiserin und Königin Maria Theresia».** *«Großer Kreuzer, 5200 T., 9000 ind. Pfk., 82 G. In Dienst gestellt seit 1910»* — and among her officers, after Förster and Kozsár, *L. Sch. L. Defranceschi, Julius*. Back to salt water, on the navy's first armoured cruiser.

**Marinedetachement in Budapest.** *«Kommandant: Freg. K. Mallinarich v. Silbergrund und Kollinensieg, Eugen … L. Sch. L. Vok, Johann … Defranceschi, Julius … Pachta-Rayhofen, Percival Gf. v.»* A naval officer posted to the Hungarian capital, four hundred kilometres from the sea.
**Number 100 in the seniority list**, in the war's first spring. Born 1879, serving since 1/7/98, rank from 1/1/09, course A.
Under **SEEOFFIZIERE**, with two decorations against his name, in the same table as Georg Ritter von Trapp.
**Still on the list.** The last rank list this archive can find him in, printed four months before the monarchy he served stopped existing. Same birth year, same service date, same seniority.

trapp.heading: And the man he entered with
trapp.text:
Two places below Julius in the seniority table of 31 August 1917 stands **«Trapp, Georg Ritt. v.»**, with a long row of decorations after his name — the submarine commander who, after the war and a second marriage, became the father of the Trapp Family Singers.

They are not friends on the evidence; they are neighbours in a table. But they are neighbours because of something real: **both entered the navy on 1 July 1898**, out of the same academy intake, and they stayed within a few lines of one another in the printed order of precedence for twenty years. Where Trapp's row fills with orders and war decorations, Julius's carries two symbols. Both were still on the list in 1918.

unknown: **Where he was born.** Not one of the 181 entries gives a birthplace — the lists record the year and not the town. Until a birth record is found he cannot be attached to Rijeka, to Bakar, or to anywhere else.
**Who his parents were.** If he is the harbour master's family, the obvious candidate generation is the household of Franciscus and Bellinich at Bakar. That is a guess with nothing under it.
**When he died.** The trail stops with the empire. Austrian, Hungarian and Croatian records after 1918 have not been searched for him.
**What his decorations were.** The symbols are printed as small devices that the OCR renders as blots. They are legible on the page images and have not been read.
citenote: 181 entries across 79 volumes. **RL** = *Rangs- und Eintheilungs-Liste der k. u. k. Kriegs-Marine* (from 1909, *Rang- und Einteilungsliste der k. u. k. Kriegsmarine*), Vienna, published two to four times a year. **SCH** = the annual *Schematismus für das k. u. k. Heer und für die k. u. k. Kriegs-Marine*. All at Hungaricana, free. Page numbers are the volume's own. Entries in the 180s–250s of the rank lists are the alphabetical index; the substantive entries are the low pages and the 120–200 band.
